cor:product-exclusion.cautions: No Lean proof is claimed. Finite computations retain the recorded evidence limits; source checking is not an independent full census.
cor:product-exclusion.conclusion: The ten-qudit state $|F_{11}\rangle$ is not Clifford-equivalent to a product across any nontrivial bipartition. The same conclusion holds for the dihedral and Borel six-qudit conic trades over $\mathbb F_7$ in Appendix~\ref{sec:finite-data}. This entropy test alone does not establish the conclusion for the six-qudit Clebsch state $|F_7\rangle$.
cor:product-exclusion.hypotheses: The field, dimensional and configuration/noise assumptions stated below.

lem:product-ceiling.cautions: No Lean proof is claimed. Finite computations retain the recorded evidence limits; source checking is not an independent full census.
lem:product-ceiling.conclusion: For a pure state in dimension $D$ with an orthogonal unitary Pauli basis, $M_2\leq\log((D+1)/2)$. Thus a pure product on blocks of $a$ and $k-a$ prime-dimensional qudits satisfies \begin{equation} M_2\leq\log\frac{(p^a+1)(p^{k-a}+1)}4. \end{equation}
lem:product-ceiling.hypotheses: The field, dimensional and configuration/noise assumptions stated below.

lem:waring.cautions: No Lean proof is claimed. Finite computations retain the recorded evidence limits; source checking is not an independent full census.
lem:waring.conclusion: The weighted linear-form cubic ranks obey $9\leq r(F_7)\leq13$ and $15\leq r(F_{11})\leq21$. The rank-nine lower bound also holds for any homogeneous cubic phase on six qudits Clifford-equivalent to $|F_7\rangle$.
lem:waring.hypotheses: The field, dimensional and configuration/noise assumptions stated below.

prop:conic-input.cautions: No Lean proof is claimed. Finite computations retain the recorded evidence limits; source checking is not an independent full census.
prop:conic-input.conclusion: For the stated matchings the construction has distinct points, $\dim L=p$, and $\dim L^{\circ2}=2p-1$. It gives $[[14,6,2]]_7$ and $[[22,10,2]]_{11}$. In invertible logical coordinates, consisting of a scalar coordinate $s$ and five quartic or nine octavic coordinates, the phases are \begin{equation} F_7=4sI+3J,\qquad F_{11}=4sI_2+2I_3. \end{equation} Here $I=ae-4bd+3c^2$ and $J=\det\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b&c\\b&c&d\\c&d&e\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ are binary-quartic invariants. For the binary octavic $f(S,T)=\sum_{i=0}^8\binom8i z_iS^{8-i}T^i$, $I_2=(f,f)_8$ and $I_3=((f,f)_4,f)_8$ use normalized transvectants.
prop:conic-input.hypotheses: The field, dimensional and configuration/noise assumptions stated below.

prop:shadow.cautions: No Lean proof is claimed. Finite computations retain the recorded evidence limits; source checking is not an independent full census.
prop:shadow.conclusion: Over $\mathbb F_{11}$ the stabilizer $A_5$ of the base matching acts on the logical space as $\one\oplus V_4\oplus V_5$. The restriction to its unique five-dimensional constituent is, in the recorded coordinates, \[ 8\det\begin{pmatrix}v_0&v_1&v_2\\v_1&v_2&v_3\\v_2&v_3&v_4\end{pmatrix}. \] Here $v_0,\ldots,v_4$ are new linear coordinates on $A$. The restriction is a chordal member of the invariant pencil. At ranks $0,3,4,5$, the chordal and conference censuses are respectively \[ (1,120,27720,133210),\qquad (1,300,22260,138490). \] Thus their five-qudit phase states are not Clifford-equivalent. At $p=7$ the restriction $s=0$ in \eqref{eq:normal-forms} is $3J$. Reversing the sheets sends $U_F$ to $U_F^{-1}$, a Clifford-conjugate gate. Let $q$ be the involution on $A$ induced by the permutation $(01)(24)(35)$ of these ordered pairs. With actual representatives $h$ and $h_2=h\circ q$, $q$ exchanges the two chordal members and gives a linear Clifford equivalence of their five-qudit states.
prop:shadow.hypotheses: The field, dimensional and configuration/noise assumptions stated below.

prop:spectra.cautions: No Lean proof is claimed. Finite computations retain the recorded evidence limits; source checking is not an independent full census.
prop:spectra.conclusion: The nonzero entries of the vector rank distributions for the two conic phases are \[ \begin{array}{c|rrrrr} p=7:\ r&0&3&4&5&6\\\hline N_r&1&48&2940&26502&88158 \end{array} \] \[ \begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr} p=11:\ r&0&5&6&7&8&9&10\\\hline N_r&1&120&14520&80520&21442960&2387485210&23528401270. \end{array} \] In each case the minimum positive rank is $(p-1)/2$, attained on exactly $p+1$ projective points. In the binary-form coordinates these are $s=0$ and the perfect $(p-3)$rd powers. In particular, \[ M_2(F_7)=\log\frac{1977326743}{78835},\qquad M_2(F_{11})=\log\frac{11^{19}}{7151076991}. \]
prop:spectra.hypotheses: The field, dimensional and configuration/noise assumptions stated below.

prop:translation.cautions: No Lean proof is claimed. Finite computations retain the recorded evidence limits; source checking is not an independent full census.
prop:translation.conclusion: These sheets define a strength-two trade with affine span $V$ and $\dim L=p$. Its code is $[[2p,p-1,2]]_p$, and its logical cubic is \begin{equation} F(u)=-3u(t)q(u),\qquad q(u)=\sum_i u(a_i)^2\quad(u\in V^*). \end{equation} The quadratic form $q$ has rank $p-2$. Moreover $\dim L^{\circ2}=2p-1$; every preserving physical cubic weight is a scalar multiple of the sheet-sign vector.
prop:translation.hypotheses: The field, dimensional and configuration/noise assumptions stated below.

thm:factory.cautions: No Lean proof is claimed. Finite computations retain the recorded evidence limits; source checking is not an independent full census.
thm:factory.conclusion: Under~\eqref{eq:noise}, for every $0<\delta\leq0.01$, let $q$ be the native factory's output block infidelity. Its expected raw consumption is less than $16.116$. Every separate construction in the sign-only menu with block infidelity at most $q$ costs at least $54$ raw inputs per output; in the weighted relaxation it costs at least $36$. Feasible separate constructions meeting this target exist throughout the interval.
thm:factory.hypotheses: The field, dimensional and configuration/noise assumptions stated below.

thm:hessian.cautions: No Lean proof is claimed. Finite computations retain the recorded evidence limits; source checking is not an independent full census.
thm:hessian.conclusion: Let $p\geq5$, and set $r(v)=\rk H_F(v)$ and $N_r=\#\{v:r(v)=r\}$. Then \begin{equation} |\langle F|X(v)Z(w)|F\rangle|= \begin{cases}p^{-r(v)/2},&w\in\im H_F(v),\\0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases} \end{equation} Consequently \begin{equation} M_\alpha(|F\rangle)=\frac{1}{1-\alpha} \log\left(p^{-k}\sum_{r=0}^kN_rp^{(1-\alpha)r}\right). \end{equation}
thm:hessian.hypotheses: The field, dimensional and configuration/noise assumptions stated below.

thm:trade-code.cautions: No Lean proof is claimed. Finite computations retain the recorded evidence limits; source checking is not an independent full census.
thm:trade-code.conclusion: Suppose $n=2p$, $k=p-1$, and $\dim L=p$. Then the CSS code with X-stabilizer space $S=\langle\one\rangle$ and Z-stabilizer space $L^\perp$ has parameters $[[2p,p-1,2]]_p$. The signed transversal operation $\bigotimes_i M_{\epsilon_i}$, where $M_c|z\rangle=\omega^{cz^3}|z\rangle$, induces the logical diagonal gate \begin{equation} U_F|u\rangle=\omega^{F(u)}|u\rangle,\qquad F(u)=\sum_i\epsilon_i(x_i^Tu)^3. \end{equation} More generally, for $S\subseteq L$, a physical cubic with weights $w_i$ is constant on every coset of $S$ in $L$ if and only if $\sum_i w_i s_i b_i c_i=0$ for all $s\in S$ and $b,c\in L$. For $S=\langle\one\rangle$ this condition is $w\perp L^{\circ2}$.
thm:trade-code.hypotheses: The field, dimensional and configuration/noise assumptions stated below.
